episode_title: Five Minute Friday: The Real Strategy Behind Selling Through Inventory

real_qa.q: What is the complete inventory life cycle strategy for boutique owners before launching new products?
real_qa.r: Before a collection hits your website, think about the plan for inventory: tease it by showing boxes coming in and unboxing, launch at full price, then continue marketing it with different styling approaches like flat lays and on-body photos. After launch, keep showing the product over and over through organic marketing and paid ads targeting people who visited, added to cart, or engaged with content. As the collection ages, identify winners and slower pieces, then get creative with styling, bundling, or featuring on lives before strategically marking down. The entire life cycle includes teasing, launching at full price, continuous marketing and retargeting, creative repositioning of slower sellers, strategic markdowns, and eventual exit.

real_qa.q: Why should boutique owners avoid immediately discounting slow-selling inventory after launch?
real_qa.r: Sometimes a product doesn't need a discount, it just needs better marketing. Before immediately marking pieces down, get creative by styling them differently, bundling something, pairing a slower top with a best-selling jean, featuring it on a live, or making it part of a themed collection. Inventory sitting around forever costs money by taking up space on racks and website, and tying up capital that could go toward new products.

Paid ads can do heavy lifting by continuing to get products in front of customers who visited that product, added it to their cart, engaged with your content, or have shopped on your website. Just because you have seen something 15 times doesn't mean your customer has—social media isn't showing every post to every follower and email list isn't opening every email, so you have to keep showing up with it.

real_qa.r: Instead of panic-marking everything at 40% off two weeks after launch, decide ahead of time how long you're willing to give inventory valuable space in your business and what you'll do at every stage. The goal is to have an exit strategy rather than panic. Ordering inventory isn't the strategy—selling through it is.
